title: Profit Maxing And Social Anti-Fragility

Profit Maxing And Social Anti-Fragility

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 18 Aug 2026

F. Scott Fitzgerald once wrote that “holding two opposite thoughts at the same time is the test of a first-rate intelligence”. With that criteria in mind, many investors we talk to are, when it comes to China, very intelligent. Indeed, the same person, in the same conversation, will sometimes explain that the Chinese economy is a house of cards that will crumble at the slightest nudge. And then, a few sentences later, also explain that China is the most dangerous threat Western liberal democracies have ever faced.On our side, not being smart enough to hold those two polar opposite thoughts simultaneously, we like to point out that thinking of collapse, and threat, when looking at China might be counterproductive. Instead, we should start off by acknowledging that while Western countries, and especially the United States, are optimized to generate the greatest amount of growth, and profits, China, because of its own tragic history and its “century of humiliation,” is first and foremost optimized to deliver social stability (see The Quid Pro Quo That Wasn’t).
